prerequisites: Knowledge of mechanics, strength of materials, kinetics, and kinematics

learning_outcomes.text: Students know small and special vehicles in different variants and designs.
Students have the necessary basic knowledge required for the development of small and special vehicles.
Students are able to evaluate and explain vehicles from the taught area.
They know the different vehicles from the micromobility and special vehicle segment and can demonstrate the differences and parallels to conventional vehicles.
Students also apply subject-specific skills and abilities in familiar and unfamiliar contexts.
Students know the differences and parallels of such vehicles compared to conventional passenger cars.
Students can integrate new technologies based on the acquired knowledge and derive scientific innovations from them.
Students can convey their ideas to colleagues and superiors in discussions and present them plausibly.
Students can assess and evaluate existing and future challenges in mobility.

syllabus_topics: Vehicle concepts besides the classic passenger car
Micromobility with small and miniature vehicles
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is a term paper. The term paper involves a semester-long project work with milestone and final presentations, as well as a project report of at least 30 pages.
